solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Heroic digital photo?

parts.note: E is the usual prefix for anything electronic or digital, as in e-book
a pic is a casual word for a photograph

explanation.surface: A query whether a snapshot taken on a phone counts as heroic.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective describes deeds on a grand, heroic scale, like those in an epic poem.

clue.text: Cold frost on American peninsula

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rime is a white frost of frozen fog droplets

explanation.surface: A cold snap brings frost to a peninsula in the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is the peninsula jutting into the Black Sea, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Menu in Paddington's 'as much as you can eat', according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two phrases trade places

parts.words: as much as you can eat
parts.note: a fill is as much as one wants or can eat, as in eat your fill
Paddington is the marmalade-loving bear of children's books, so his fill is the fill of a bear

explanation.surface: A menu that seems to promise the famous bear all he can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington's fill becomes FILL OF BEAR; swapping the F and B sounds gives the answer, with FEAR heard as FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is an old-fashioned term for the list of dishes a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Main course initially covered in curry

indicators.note: in a down answer a letter covered by another word sits beneath it, so the course letter goes below the curry

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a wok-like dish, popular in Birmingham

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of course is used

explanation.surface: A main course arriving smothered in curry sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main course' reads as one dish, but Main is the definition: the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is a sea, and the main is a poetic word for the sea or open ocean.

clue.text: 1970s leader the last character to be embraced by retiring Archdeacon Basil?

indicators.note: to be embraced by means the letter goes inside the reversed pair of words
retiring means going backwards, so the archdeacon and basil words are read in reverse

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
basil is a herb
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A churchman named Basil, about to retire, hugs the final person in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid Brezhnev led the Soviet Union through the 1970s as General Secretary of its Communist Party.

clue.text: Second hand, put up for exchange

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word for hand is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a paw is a jocular word for a hand

explanation.surface: A second-hand item is offered as a trade rather than for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another, the same idea as an exchange.

clue.text: Travelling quickly, yacht finally berthed?

definitions.meaning: going along at speed, as a car does on an open road
a cryptic picture: the closing letter of yacht tied up in a place where boats are kept

explanation.surface: A yacht speeds along and is at last tied up in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic picture rather than a plain definition: the last letter of yacht, T, berthed inside MOORING gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoring is informal for going at speed, as in 'we were really motoring along'.

clue.text: Flog trade secret, losing a measure of respect with the kids

definitions.text: measure of respect with the kids

indicators.note: to flog is to beat, so the letters of the phrase are knocked into a new order
losing says the letter a is dropped from the jumbled phrase

explanation.surface: Someone sells a trade secret and loses the respect of young people.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'Flog' at first reads as 'sell'. Remove one A from TRADE SECRET and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility among the young and fashionable, a kind of standing or esteem.

clue.text: Zoroastrian play Russia regularly censored

indicators.note: regularly censored means every other letter of the two words is struck out, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A play put on in Russia keeps getting cut by the censors.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsis are the Zoroastrian community of India, descended from Persian refugees.

clue.text: Barb exposed argument with England cricketer (paper version includes: that's turned up) in West Indian ground

indicators.note: exposed means the word barb is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument
Joe Root is an England batsman and former Test captain

explanation.surface: A cutting remark sparks a row with an England cricketer at a Caribbean ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed note is an editorial remark that the newspaper version reads differently; it plays no part in the wordplay. 'West Indian ground' suggests a cricket ground, but it means a ground powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch powder ground from the rhizome of a West Indian plant, used as a thickener.

clue.text: Legendary location in California runs out of wine

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: out of means the letter for runs is removed from the wine

parts.note: Merlot is a red wine grape and its wine
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Californian venue has run out of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's court in the Arthurian legends, a place of myth rather than history.

clue.text: It helps to get delivery from Languedoc pizzeria on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ordering a pizza delivery from a restaurant in southern France on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: A zip code is the American postal code, which helps the post office deliver mail to the right address.

clue.text: Rubbish hotel invested in downmarket coffee bar

indicators.note: invested in means the hotel letter is placed inside the cafe word

parts.note: caff is British slang for a cheap, basic cafe
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel puts money into a cheap cafe, which is a waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is husks separated from grain, so by extension worthless stuff or trash.

clue.text: Bishop in strange secrecy about father's virtual world

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the father word
strange signals that the letters of secrecy are rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A bishop shrouded in odd secrecy about his father's online world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the bishop among the jumbled letters of secrecy, so B is mixed into that pool; 'about' then wraps the result round the father word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional realm of computer networks, an imagined or virtual environment.

clue.text: Swindler in bed, suffering strain

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters of strain are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone laid up in bed with a muscle strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A con artist is a confidence trickster who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Workman and lad, unusually, in indication of trendlessness?

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of the two words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A workman and a boy, oddly, as a sign that nothing is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a random walk is a path of random steps, showing no underlying trend.

clue.text: It's used for dressing, calming abrasive wound

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, says the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment applied to a graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' and 'wound' suggest first aid; dressing is a salad dressing, and 'wound' is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsamic vinegar is a dark Italian vinegar commonly drizzled on salads as a dressing.

clue.text: Rip jagged tear beneath delicate fabric

indicators.note: in a down answer beneath places the jumbled letters below the fabric word

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric

indicators.note: jagged suggests the letters of tear are torn into a rough new order

explanation.surface: A ragged rip appears under some fine lace.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear flesh or skin roughly, a forceful kind of ripping.

clue.text: Yours truly had substance and character

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, so this is I had, contracted to I'd
an entity is something that has real existence or substance

explanation.surface: A person who had real substance and strong character.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity is the set of traits that make someone who they are, their individual nature.

clue.text: Criminal fraudster advanced to take over from old ballistics expert

indicators.note: to take over from means the new letter replaces the old one

parts.note: a rocketeer is a designer or user of rockets
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A con man rises to replace a veteran weapons expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest racket such as extortion or fraud.

clue.text: Journalist on the up leaving ramshackle reminder of a bygone era

indicators.note: leaving means the reversed journalist letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: derelict means dilapidated and run-down

indicators.note: in a down answer on the up means the journalist word reads upwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A rising reporter quits a tumbledown relic of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is a survivor or remnant from an earlier period, a leftover of the past.

clue.text: Had moved down, securing a point?

indicators.note: securing means the jumbled letters hold the point letter inside
moved means the letters of down are shifted around

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone shifted downhill and won a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned something is to have possessed it, so had in its past sense of possession.

clue.text: It's used to irritate; there is a point to it

definitions.text: there is a point to it
definitions.meaning: a sewing or hypodermic pin has a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Something designed to annoy, which at least has a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is a sharp-tipped tool, and to needle is to irritate someone persistently.

clue.text: On Broadway, section of theatre role showcasing Manuel's trademark reply?

indicators.note: showcasing means the role word displays the reply set inside it

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
Manuel, the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, constantly answers 'Que?'

explanation.surface: A Broadway role that shows off a comic waiter's catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In American theatres the parquet is the ground-floor seating area, what the British call the stalls.

clue.text: It meanders, surreally, off and on

indicators.note: off and on means letters are skipped and taken in turn, starting with a skip

explanation.surface: Something winding about in a dreamlike, intermittent way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan, and rivers wind across land.

clue.text: First or second tragedy to enfold over Grace

indicators.note: to enfold means the tragedy wraps around the other letters

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
W.G. Grace was the great Victorian England cricketer

explanation.surface: First or second place, and a tragic fall for a sporting great.
explanation.definitionFit: First and second are the low gears in a car's gearbox, used for slow speeds and pulling away.

clue.text: Topless pair in competition

indicators.note: topless means the word for pair loses its top letter, which is its first in a down answer

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Two topless people take part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed, one kind of sporting competition.

clue.text: Whip with peeled sharp stick? It's purifying!

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip

indicators.note: peeled means sharp and stick each lose their outer letters, like skin removed

explanation.surface: Whipping someone with a sharpened stick presented as a purifying act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cathartic purges or cleanses the emotions, bringing release.

clue.text: Long Island city, 100 in the shade?

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Long Island, New York
LA, Los Angeles, is the usual crossword city
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A New York suburb hits a hundred degrees even in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour, a particular hue named after the flower.
